v11_changes_summary: max_concurrent_positions: 5 (v7) → 4 (single-lever sweep, bracket v7 peak FROM BELOW)
Reverts v10's two confounding levers (min_opportunistic_count 3→2, stage3_require_both True→False) back to v7's OR-logic baseline
Stage 1 unchanged at v4/v6/v7 local optimum (4 / $10M)
Purpose: characterize whether the v6→v7→v8 cap-axis (8 → 5 → 3, Sharpe -0.36 → +0.58 → -0.74) has a peak strictly at cap=5 or whether cap=4 holds residual Sharpe above zero

implementation_notes.patch_description: Single-lever sweep on max_concurrent_positions only. All v7 settings preserved except cap (5 → 4). Confirms the cap-axis U-shape geometry: v7 (cap=5) is the right ridge, v11 (cap=4) is the left descent toward v8 (cap=3, Sharpe -0.74).
implementation_notes.methodology_note: Combined Sharpe uses the v7+ canonical aggregate_metrics-style calculation (distribute pnl_pct evenly across each trade's holding_days, equal-weighted daily portfolio mean, std ddof=1, rf=5%/252, annualize sqrt(252)). The v6-era variant calculation is NOT used here — v7 verdict reproduced v4's combined_sharpe=0.358 with this method, anchoring it as the canonical methodology going forward.

baseline_a.description: S12_insider BUY-only, OPENCLAW_S15_INSIDER_OPPORTUNISTIC=0, OPENCLAW_S12_SELL_CLUSTER=0, max-hold-days=60. REUSED verbatim from v1-v10.
baseline_a.notes: Reused from v1-v10 (baseline does not depend on S15 parameters).

modified_s15_standalone.description: S15 with v11 settings (cap=4, OR-logic Stage 3, min_opp=2). OPENCLAW_S15_INSIDER_OPPORTUNISTIC=1, OPENCLAW_S12_SELL_CLUSTER=0
modified_s15_standalone.notes: v11 cap=4 IS WORSE than v7 cap=5. Standalone Sharpe FELL from v7's +0.58 to v11's -0.42 (delta -1.00 absolute). Confirms v7 cap=5 is a SHARP local peak. Per-trade avg_pnl COLLAPSED from v7's 0.0046 to v11's 0.0020 (~57% drop); trade count fell from v7's 394 to v11's 336 (only ~15% reduction); MaxDD WIDENED from v7's 4.02% to v11's 6.24%. Hit rate held flat (~0.61). Interpretation: cap=4 reaches deeper into the ranking than cap=5 without buying enough variance-reduction to compensate — the marginal trades pruned by cap=4 vs cap=5 were the higher-quality survivors, so the surviving pool quality DEGRADED rather than improved. The cap-axis curve is now characterized: v8 cap=3 (-0.74) < v11 cap=4 (-0.42) < v6 cap=8 (-0.36) < v4 cap=20 (+0.28) < v7 cap=5 (+0.58). cap=5 is a singular peak.

ablation.notes: IDENTICAL to modified_s15_standalone (byte-for-byte). Calendar-quarter Stage 2 classifier remains non-discriminating for the eleventh consecutive version. G5 fails: ablation_sharpe is NOT strictly less than modified_sharpe.

ablation_root_cause_analysis.finding: Stage 2 calendar-quarter classifier (v1 Cohen-Malloy-Pomorski 2012) remains structurally inert for the 11th consecutive version. Same DATA-property failure: per-insider sale history is too sparse for the 15-to-3-month rolling window to populate quarterly buckets, so nearly every (ticker, insider_name) pair returns 'opportunistic'.
ablation_root_cause_analysis.classifier_mechanism: classify_insider() checks for sales in a 12-month rolling window. With sparse parquet history, nearly all sellers default to 'opportunistic'.
ablation_root_cause_analysis.code_correctness: Stage 2 is correctly implemented. Inertness is a data-depth limitation, not a code bug.
ablation_root_cause_analysis.v11_cap_effect: max_concurrent_positions=4 (down from v7's 5) pruned the bottom ranks more aggressively, removing 58 trades (394 → 336, ~15% reduction). But the marginal trades pruned were apparently NOT bottom-tail noise — they were diversifying-quality fires that contributed positive Sharpe in v7. The cap-axis monotonic-tightening hypothesis is REFUTED for cap < 5: tightening past v7's cap=5 destroys signal faster than it removes noise. v8 (cap=3) is even worse (-0.74). v11 (cap=4) sits on the descending shoulder between the v7 peak and the v8 valley.

modified_combined.description: Portfolio-level Sharpe computed from union of S12 BUY trades (run_id 7f9ed076) + S15 v11 SHORT trades (run_id 4ec8492b), equal-weighted daily portfolio mirroring aggregate_metrics() in unified_backtest.py
modified_combined.methodology_note: Built daily_pnls dict from both run_ids' strategy_backtest_trades, distributed pnl_pct evenly across holding_days starting day-after-entry (calendar days), equal-weighted on each day. Sharpe = (mean - rf_daily) / std(ddof=1) * sqrt(252), rf=5%/252. Identical to aggregate_metrics() implementation in unified_backtest.py.

standalone.v11_changes_vs_v7: Single-lever sweep: max_concurrent_positions 5→4. All other v7 settings preserved. Trade count fell 394→336 (~15%; less than the v6→v7 drop of ~25% because cap=4 prunes only the tail). Per-trade avg_pnl FELL 0.0046→0.0020 (~57% drop). Standalone Sharpe COLLAPSED +0.58 → -0.42 (-1.00 absolute swing). Standalone MaxDD widened 4.02% → 6.24% (+2.2pp). Conclusion: cap=5 is a singular peak on the concentration-cap axis. Cap-axis curve fully characterized: v8 cap=3 (-0.74) < v11 cap=4 (-0.42) < v6 cap=8 (-0.36) < v4 cap=20 (+0.28) < v7 cap=5 (+0.58). cap=5 is monotonically declining in BOTH directions.

computed_suggestion_rationale: v11 cap=4 underperformed v7 cap=5 on standalone Sharpe by -1.00 absolute, confirming v7's peak is sharply singular. Three of six gates pass (G2, G4, G6), three fail (G1, G3, G5). v11 brackets v7 from below the way v8 (cap=3, Sharpe -0.74) did, with v11 sitting between v8 and v7 on the descending shoulder. Cap-axis is now fully characterized as a single-peaked U-inverted curve with maximum at cap=5; no further single-lever cap-axis exploration will improve on v7. v7 remains the global best of the 11-version sweep.
